plain: Michels suggests that some of science's great breakthroughs may have arrived like inspiration from outside, almost downloaded. His examples are Albert Einstein working out the photoelectric effect (how light knocks electrons out of metal) while bored at his desk in the Swiss patent office, the physicist Wolfgang Pauli dreaming up the structure of the hydrogen atom, Werner Heisenberg finding his matrix mathematics on the island of Helgoland, and Paul Dirac staring into a fire in Cambridge before writing his famous equation. He offers this as his own idea, and in a later episode credits the writer Jimena Canales for it, leaves out Einstein and Pauli, and adds Niels Bohr and René Descartes, which takes the pattern back to the 1600s.
